findings.title: AssignmentSource.queued is fixed at import time
findings.body: queued is declared as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. Dataclass defaults are evaluated once when the class body runs, not per instance, and datetime is not rejected as a mutable default. Every AssignmentSource built without an explicit queued value — including every AssignmentSource.from_integration() call on the inbound webhook path — therefore shares one timestamp captured when the worker process imported the module. to_dict() copies that value into the Celery payload, so the field does not record when the assignment was queued and cannot order or expire the rapid successive assignee updates this PR is about. Use field(default_factory=timezone.now).

findings.title: Outbound assignee task payload embeds a raw datetime
findings.body: sync_group_assignee_outbound passes assignment_source.to_dict() into sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async. to_dict() is dataclasses.asdict(), so assignment_source_dict contains a live datetime under queued. Standard JSON encoding of that payload raises TypeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable. apply_async is called from GroupAssignee.assign and deassign, which sync_group_assignee_inbound now always reaches for integration-driven assignee changes, so a JSON task serializer fails the inbound webhook and never enqueues outbound sync to other integrations. Encoders that stringify datetimes do not raise, but AssignmentSource.from_dict only does cls(**input_dict) and does not parse ISO-8601, so queued arrives on the worker as a str. Store queued with isoformat() (or a numeric timestamp) and parse it in from_dict.

findings.title: Unparseable assignment source fails open and restarts the loop
findings.body: If assignment_source_dict is present but AssignmentSource.from_dict returns None, the task still calls should_sync("outbound_assignee", None) and, when outbound assignee sync is enabled, writes the assignee back to the external issue. from_dict returns None on any TypeError or ValueError (missing fields, unexpected keys, a queued value that cannot be constructed) and does not log. A source payload that fails to parse is then indistinguishable from a Sentry-originated assignment, which is exactly the path that updates the originating integration and restarts the sync cycle. When a source dict was supplied and cannot be reconstructed, outbound sync should be skipped rather than performed.

findings.title: Cycle-break tests miss the inbound webhook path
findings.body: The new test only calls GroupAssignee.objects.assign with an AssignmentSource and asserts that the same integration's sync_assignee_outbound is not invoked. Nothing calls sync_group_assignee_inbound, which is the webhook entry point that must attach AssignmentSource.from_integration. Removing that argument would restore the production loop and still pass CI. Deassign with a matching source is also untested, and there is no two-integration case proving a different linked integration still receives the outbound update. tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py never round-trips to_dict() through JSON and never checks that two instances get different queued timestamps, so the shared default and the non-serializable task payload are invisible.
